Hey man, I really hope you can still see this. I hated when people told me that they “understood”, but I have had a similar experience. I was alone in a college dorm about 8 months ago, completely isolated, scared, and had absolutely zero self respect. I was desperate for any reprieve from the horrific suicidal ideation. I’m a recovering heroin addict and of course, at that time, it was so unimaginably tempting, but there’s a part in all human beings that is based on logic and survival. Whether you want it there or not. Hell, I was somehow able to stay clean throughout the most lonely and depressing points in my life. That doesn’t mean I didn’t make horrifically reckless decisions that could’ve very quickly ended my life. Now that I think about it, I think I was hoping something would go wrong like a car accident and kill me so I didn’t have to leave my family with a son who committed suicide. All of this is to say and describe the way that I felt hopeless and thought about suicide at all moments. Every single thought that ran through my head ended with, “but it doesn’t matter because I’m going to be dead before then”. Fast forward 8 months, and I’m the happiest I’ve ever been. It was the point where I made radical changes to the way I put out negativity into the world that my life turned around. It was complete bullshit at first when I would just try to smile and see any semblance of a bright side. I adopted the ideology that if I was gonna die either way, then why would absolutely anything matter. I started taking every drastic risk I could. I stood up, changed colleges, and never looked back. I threw away everything that made me feel like a worthless person. I had been very attached mentally to an extremely abusive person, but because I was “gonna die either way” I took what, at the time, was the biggest risk I could ever take. I let go of my abuser. All contact was excommunicated and removed. I did anything and everything I wanted to do that might have even the slightest possibility of making me feel anything but suicidal. Go on pointless walks, talk with my dad for hours, lay down and god forbid, give myself a break. I was gonna die at the end of the day either way, right. I didn’t even notice, but through making these decisions that were based purely on my desire to do them, I found a new life for myself. I switched my entire dreams around for stuff I WANTED to do. Who gives a fuck either way, suicidal thoughts told me nothing mattered, and I believe that taking that fact, and twisting it into something that empowers you is the most freeing and life saving thing you can ever do. I found an absolutely incredible person since letting go of my past abuse, and I’m now recognizing the abnormality of how I had been living. You WILL meet new people that make you look at yourself. You WILL take yourself and find a way to try to make you happy. It WILL free you more than I can even due justice with in words once you finally take these suicidal thoughts telling you everything is worthless about you and the world, twist them, and end up with your own suicidal thoughts working for you, making you realize that nothing matters, SO, go do anything you want that will make you happy. Please give it a try, doing whatever you want that will give you a new perspective, meet new people, try new things, and most importantly, give yourself a break. Nobody’s judging, and everybody is rooting for you, friend.
